steps.note: Create the trigger function that keeps amount and total equal on every insert/update, whichever of the two the writer sets (old app writes amount, new app writes total).
steps.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION orders_sync_total() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $f$ BEGIN IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN IF NEW.total IS NULL THEN NEW.total := NEW.amount; ELSIF NEW.amount IS NULL THEN NEW.amount := NEW.total; END IF; ELSE IF NEW.amount IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.amount AND NEW.total IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OLD.total THEN NEW.total := NEW.amount; ELSIF NEW.total IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.total AND NEW.amount IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OLD.amount THEN NEW.amount := NEW.total; END IF; END IF; RETURN NEW; END $f$;

steps.note: Add nullable column total numeric(10,2) (metadata-only, no rewrite) and the sync trigger in one transaction, so every row written from now on has total. The lock is taken with a 200 ms lock_timeout and retried, so app queries never queue behind it for long.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE tries int := 0; BEGIN LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '200ms', true); ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS total numeric(10,2); CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER orders_sync_total BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON orders FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION orders_sync_total(); EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN tries := tries + 1; IF tries >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.5); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Backfill total = amount for ids 1..1,000,000 in 250k-row batches, each committed on its own (row locks only; the app never updates existing orders).
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; UPDATE orders SET total = amount WHERE id > 0 AND id <= 250000 AND total IS NULL; SELECT pg_sleep(0.5); UPDATE orders SET total = amount WHERE id > 250000 AND id <= 500000 AND total IS NULL; SELECT pg_sleep(0.5); UPDATE orders SET total = amount WHERE id > 500000 AND id <= 750000 AND total IS NULL; SELECT pg_sleep(0.5); UPDATE orders SET total = amount WHERE id > 750000 AND id <= 1000000 AND total IS NULL; SELECT pg_sleep(0.5);

steps.note: Backfill whatever is left above id 10,000,000 (orders inserted before the trigger existed; later ones already have total).
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; UPDATE orders SET total = amount WHERE id > 10000000 AND total IS NULL;

steps.note: Add CHECK (total IS NOT NULL) as NOT VALID: brief lock, no scan, retried on lock timeout.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE tries int := 0; BEGIN LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '200ms', true); ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_total_not_null CHECK (total IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN tries := tries + 1; IF tries >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.5); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Validate the check: a full scan under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, which does not block reads or writes. Fails (and stops the plan) if any row still has a NULL total.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_total_not_null;

steps.note: SET NOT NULL on total (Postgres proves it from the validated check, so no scan), then drop the redundant check. Brief lock, retried.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE tries int := 0; BEGIN LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '200ms', true); ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN total SET NOT NULL; ALTER TABLE orders DROP CONSTRAINT orders_total_not_null; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN tries := tries + 1; IF tries >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.5); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Verify every row has total = amount before switching the app; stops the plan if not.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; DO $$ BEGIN IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders WHERE total IS DISTINCT FROM amount) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'total and amount differ'; END IF; END $$;

steps.note: Roll the app over to read and write total. While old pods (amount) and new pods (total) coexist during the rolling update, the trigger fills whichever column a writer leaves out, so both stay correct.
Let terminating old pods finish their in-flight requests and close their database connections.
Make sure no connection is still running the old app's SQL (which names amount); wait up to 60 s, otherwise stop before anything is dropped.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE n int; BEGIN FOR i IN 1..60 LOOP SELECT count(*) INTO n FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE pid <> pg_backend_pid() AND query ~ '(customer_id, amount, status|, amount AS amount|SELECT id, amount AS)'; EXIT WHEN n = 0; PERFORM pg_sleep(1); END LOOP; IF n > 0 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'old app version still connected (% sessions)', n; END IF; END $$;

steps.note: Check total = amount for every row one last time, then drop the sync trigger and the amount column in one short metadata-only transaction (lock retried).
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; DO $$ BEGIN IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders WHERE total IS DISTINCT FROM amount) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'total and amount differ'; END IF; END $$; DO $$ DECLARE tries int := 0; BEGIN LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '200ms', true); DROP TRIGGER orders_sync_total ON orders; ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN amount; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN tries := tries + 1; IF tries >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.5); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Drop the trigger function and refresh planner statistics.
steps.sql: DROP FUNCTION orders_sync_total(); ANALYZE orders;
